nodes.label: Conventional Commits + mandatory ETG ticket
nodes.rationale: Commit messages must be Conventional Commits with a mandatory ETG-<number> ticket reference so every change is traceable to a ticket; enforced redundantly by a local pre-commit hook and by CI so neither a rushed local commit nor a bypassed hook can slip through.

nodes.label: Guardrails as cost control
nodes.rationale: Framing lint/test/commit-message/secret-scanning gates as 'guardrails as cost control': catching automatable mistakes with hooks and CI instead of spending model reasoning and reviewer attention on the same class of error every time. The phrase is used near-verbatim in both ci.yml and .pre-commit-config.yaml.

nodes.label: No-hardcoded-credentials gate
nodes.rationale: A dedicated check (scripts/check_no_secrets.py) blocks any tracked file from containing a hardcoded Snowflake account identifier or other credential, run both locally via pre-commit and in CI, because the project's central rule is that connection details come only from environment variables, never a tracked file.

nodes.label: A-prefix 'Adjust bad debt' rows
nodes.rationale: Three rows with an 'A' InvoiceNo prefix ('Adjust bad debt') are non-revenue like the well-known 'C'-prefix cancellations, but are easy to miss because a naive `not like 'C%'` filter passes every test, and the three rows' signed amounts (+1, -2) nearly cancel out — a leaked total looks almost right instead of obviously wrong. Illustrates that a prefix convention observed in a few rows is a pattern, not a verified rule.

nodes.label: Bronze layer
nodes.rationale: Bronze is a faithful, untouched copy of the source so every later transformation decision is auditable against something nobody has touched; hence no cleaning, casting, filtering, dedup, or reorder, and dtype=str at read time so pandas cannot silently coerce CustomerID to float64.

nodes.label: Force dtype=str on Bronze read
nodes.rationale: pd.read_excel with dtype=str is mandatory, not stylistic: without it pandas infers CustomerID as float64 because ~25% of the column is blank, silently turning '17850' into '17850.0' in the warehouse — a transformation nobody chose.

nodes.label: Four-beat demo structure
nodes.rationale: The live session is four beats: Beat 1 commits the harness with no pipeline code yet; Beats 2-3 build Bronze and profile with Cortex under human supervision, catching real defects; Beat 4 discards that supervised work, branches fresh, and lets one long prompt build the entire pipeline unattended. The comparison is deliberately unfair to demonstrate that the harness, not model capability, is what changed.

nodes.label: Gold layer
nodes.rationale: Gold is purpose-built per question and materialized as tables because a dashboard queries it directly; it excludes non-revenue rows only by referencing Silver's named flags, never by re-deriving a rule inline, so there is one definition of each rule.

nodes.label: The harness
nodes.rationale: The harness (CLAUDE.md + AGENTS.md + skills + hooks + tests) is deliberately committed before any pipeline code exists, so Beat 4's single unattended prompt can reproduce, unassisted, the same corrections a human reviewer made by hand in Beats 2-3 — the thesis being that trust is engineered via context, not bought with a bigger model.

nodes.label: Silver layer
nodes.rationale: Silver is where judgment lives: types are cast defensively with TRY_CAST, exact duplicates are deduped once, and every row-excluding/flagging rule is named, documented, and tested rather than implied — Silver flags but never filters.
